neighbourhoods.name: Brentwood town centre
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian and Edwardian houses, purpose-built flats and newer apartment blocks near the station and High Street.

neighbourhoods.name: Shenfield
neighbourhoods.housing: A commuter area of large detached and semi-detached inter-war and post-war houses, with flats near the Elizabeth line station.

neighbourhoods.name: Hutton
neighbourhoods.housing: Mainly post-war and 1960s semis, bungalows and some former council estates.

neighbourhoods.name: Warley
neighbourhoods.housing: Inter-war semis, the former Warley Hospital converted into flats and houses, and newer infill homes.

neighbourhoods.name: Ingatestone
neighbourhoods.housing: A village with period cottages on the High Street and post-war and modern family houses around it.

neighbourhoods.name: Doddinghurst
neighbourhoods.housing: A village of chalet bungalows, detached houses and some post-war homes.

neighbourhoods.name: Herongate and Ingrave
neighbourhoods.housing: Small villages of period cottages and larger detached houses in Green Belt countryside.

neighbourhoods.name: Pilgrims Hatch
neighbourhoods.housing: A suburb of post-war semis, terraces and bungalows north-west of the town.

housing: Brentwood is a mostly owner-occupied commuter borough on the Elizabeth line, with house prices well above the regional average. Private renting grew faster here than across the region between 2011 and 2021, reaching about one in six households. Rented homes are mainly flats and apartments near Brentwood and Shenfield stations and family houses in the suburbs, with large detached homes in Shenfield and the villages. Much of the borough is Green Belt, so new building is limited and mostly infill or conversions.
checkinTips: Purpose-built and converted flats near Brentwood and Shenfield stations: photograph communal doors, entry phones and bike and bin stores, and count every key and fob.
Large detached houses in Shenfield and the villages: photograph driveways, gates, garages and garden lighting as well as the rooms.
Flats in converted older buildings such as the Warley Hospital site: note shared areas, parking permits and any service-charge rules on decoration.
Chalet bungalows in Doddinghurst and Pilgrims Hatch: photograph the eaves storage and sloping ceilings for damp or condensation.
Period cottages in Ingatestone: photograph open fireplaces, timber windows and uneven floors so their existing condition is on record.
Gardens backing onto Green Belt fields: photograph fences, hedges and gates, which often need repair after winter.
tenantHelp: Tenants can contact Brentwood Borough Council's private housing team about disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions; it can inspect and take action against landlords.
